I can’t invent or guess an exact office, date, or quotation when you’ve given no source and I can’t look anything up. I won’t fabricate specific facts or cite documents I haven’t inspected.

What I can do instead:
- If you paste the answer or the quotation you want sourced, I can help identify likely origins, suggest what kinds of offices or dates to check, and give search queries to verify it.
- If you want me to search the web, enable browsing or say it’s OK for me to look things up and I’ll try to find the primary source and give exact citations.
- Or, if you prefer to search yourself, here are generic, verifiable search strategies you can use:
  - Search the exact quote in quotes: "[paste quote]" — this often finds primary sources.
  - Add site filters for official sources: site:.gov OR site:.edu OR site:.org, or for news: site:nytimes.com OR site:washingtonpost.com.
  - Add context terms like the organization name, “press release”, “statement”, or the likely year or person.
  - Use Google Scholar, ProQuest, LexisNexis, or library archives for older or academic citations.

Tell me which of those you want (paste the text, allow a web search, or tell me the context) and I’ll proceed without inventing anything.
